labels.macosMember: Access: This Mac signs in as you
labels.macosAdmin: Access: This Mac signs in as you, a super administrator
labels.macBody: This is equivalent to entering your username and password on this Mac: it can access the same media libraries and record your viewing progress. Only approve the pairing code shown on the Mac in front of you.
labels.memberTitle: Access: The same permissions as you
labels.memberBody: The program on this machine can act as you and do everything you can do on the website, including all capabilities the administrator has granted you. Only approve if you know what program is running on this machine.
labels.adminTitle: Access: The same full access as you
labels.adminBody: The program on this machine can do everything you can do on the website, including deleting media files. Only approve if you know what program is running on this machine.
labels.manualTranscodeBody: A program holding this token can only claim and run transcoding jobs. It cannot view or change your subscriptions, media library or settings. The token does not expire automatically and can only be revoked here.
labels.manualFullBody: A program holding this token can do everything you can do on the website, including deleting media files. The token does not expire automatically and can only be revoked here. Store it only on machines you control.
labels.revokeCli: The command line on this machine will lose access immediately. Run mclaw login again to pair and regain access.
labels.revokeWorker: This transcoder will disconnect immediately and stop active transcodes. Pair it again in the transcoder to regain access.
labels.revokeManual: Programs holding this token will lose access immediately. The token cannot be restored; create a new one to regain access.
labels.revokeJellyfin: This player will sign out immediately and stop active playback. Sign in again in the player to regain access.
labels.revokePaired: This device will lose access immediately. Pair it again to regain access.
labels.revokeLogin: This device will sign out immediately and stop active playback. Enter the password again to sign in.

sites.protectionHint: Site protection is on: subscriptions will not download torrents from this site. Manual searches and downloads remain available.
sites.openSite: Open the site in a new window

sites.reduceOrder: Remove torrents from lowest to highest upload efficiency: dead and inefficient torrents first, efficient torrents last
sites.reduceRetention: Tasks within their retention period are kept until that period ends

sites.adjustBoostHint: Reducing the budget removes pool tasks and their data from lowest to highest upload efficiency until usage is within the new budget. Tasks are kept until their retention period ends.

sites.retentionHint: H&R protection: use at least the site’s required seeding period. Use 0 for sites without an H&R requirement.
sites.changedDownloaderHint: Changes apply to newly fetched torrents. Existing tasks stay in their original downloader until removed from the pool.
sites.downloaderHint: Send boosting torrents to this downloader. It can differ from the default subscription downloader to avoid queue contention.

importWatch.title: Automatic import
importWatch.description: Watch download folders and organize completed downloads into your library
importWatch.removeHint: Only folder watching stops. The source folder and files already imported are kept.
importWatch.disabledHint: While disabled, download folders are not watched and completed downloads are not organized into the library automatically.
importWatch.intro: Watch a download folder and automatically identify completed downloads, rename them as “Title (Year)”, and organize them into a library or custom folder. Completion is confirmed by the downloader, or by a stable file that passes probing. Source files stay in place: hard links use no extra space and support continued seeding; copying works across disks. Set your downloader’s save location to the source folder to organize completed downloads automatically.
importWatch.loadFailed: Could not load automatic import settings
importWatch.emptyHint: Leave this empty if you do not need automatic organization from downloads into a library.
importWatch.importedDetail: ({entries, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}} · {files, plural, one {# file} other {# files}})
importWatch.entriesFailed: Could not load the list. Please try again.
importWatch.pendingHint: These entries could not be identified automatically. They are not retried and do not raise errors. Search and assign an identity to organize an entry into the library immediately. Ignore items you do not want to organize, such as extras, personal recordings, or files managed by another tool.
importWatch.browseSource: Browse and choose a server folder…
importWatch.downloaderFolders: Choose a downloader folder, then browse further to select a subfolder if needed:
importWatch.sourceHint: Must not overlap any library root; libraries scan and manage their own contents. Subscription and manual downloads are sent here using the path MovieClaw sees. If your downloader runs in another container or host and sees different paths, configure path mappings in Settings → Downloaders first to avoid saving to the wrong location.
importWatch.hardlinkHint: Uses no extra space and preserves source seeding; requires the same filesystem as the destination library’s primary root
importWatch.copyHint: Works across disks; takes time and uses space for both copies
importWatch.hardlinkCheckHint: Saving checks whether the source and destination (a library’s primary root or a custom folder) share a filesystem. If they are on different disks, you will be prompted to use copying.
importWatch.copyCheckHint: Use copying when the source and destination are on different disks.
importWatch.autoHint: Choose a library by collection scope after identifying a title; otherwise use the default library for that type
importWatch.otherLibraryHint: Move files unchanged into the default Other library without identification or renaming; you choose its contents
importWatch.customFolderHint: Organize files into a chosen folder without adding them to a library. Movies and TV series are identified and renamed; Other files are moved unchanged. Use this when another step, such as uploading or transferring files, is needed before library import.
importWatch.noLibraries: No libraries yet. Create one from the Library page first.
importWatch.browseDestination: Choose a folder for organized files…
importWatch.kindHint: Identification needs to know whether these are movies or TV series because naming and episode parsing differ
importWatch.otherKindHint: Move files into this folder unchanged, without identification or renaming; you choose its contents
importWatch.autoDestinationHint: Automatic routing: distribute identified titles by each library’s collection scope, such as animation into an anime library. Unmatched titles go to the default library for their type. Subscription downloads always use the subscription’s library. Only one automatic routing rule is allowed per type.
importWatch.customOtherHint: Custom folder (Other): move entries unchanged into this folder without adding them to a library. Files are scanned into an Other library if later placed under its root. The folder must not overlap a library root or watched source. Only one custom folder rule is allowed per type.
importWatch.customDestinationHint: Custom folder: identify and rename downloaded files into this folder without adding them to a library. Use this when cloud uploading, file transfer or manual review is needed first. Files are scanned into a library if later placed under its root. The folder must not overlap a library root or watched source. Only one custom folder rule is allowed per type.
importWatch.fixedDestinationHint: Specific library: always import this folder’s contents into the selected library’s primary root.
importWatch.processExistingHint: Identify and organize files already in the folder
importWatch.skipExistingHint: Only process downloads that appear after the rule takes effect
importWatch.existingProcessingHint: Existing files will also be identified and organized into the library. Unrecognized entries appear under Needs attention, where you can assign identities or ignore them individually.
importWatch.existingSkippingHint: Entries already in the folder when the rule takes effect are marked Ignored, without organization or errors. Only new downloads are processed. Ignored entries can be resumed from the list at any time. Use this when another tool manages existing content.

scrape.title: Metadata and organization
scrape.description: Global defaults for posters, descriptions, naming and folder organization
scrape.metadataPrimaryHint: Uses the first metadata language; image selection follows when it changes
scrape.originalLanguageHint: The work’s original audio language, detected per title (Korean for Parasite, Japanese for Japanese animation)
scrape.textlessHint: Clean artwork without embedded text (TMDB language marked as null)
scrape.originalHint: Store every image at its original TMDB size for maximum detail on all devices
scrape.standardHint: Clear on all devices; smaller portraits and posters save about 40% of storage
scrape.compactHint: Enough for phones and the web; stills and portraits may look soft on TV
scrape.customHint: Choose a TMDB size for posters, backdrops, stills and portraits separately
scrape.addAndReorder: Choose an option above, then reorder it here
scrape.sharedNamingHint: Shared by movies and TV shows
scrape.noPathSeparators: Path separators are not allowed (the directory structure is fixed)
scrape.namingHint: Directory and file names used when organizing and importing. Leave blank for the default template. Missing fields and their adjacent brackets collapse automatically. The fixed structure is entry directory / season directory / file.
scrape.importTokensHint: Site and original filename are available only for files imported through MovieClaw. They are empty for existing files found by scanning and collapse automatically.
scrape.movieExample: Movie · Dune: Part Two (2024) · 2160p DV TrueHD Atmos · BluRay FRDS
scrape.episodeExample: TV show · Kite (2017) Season 1 Episode 3 · 1080p SDR AAC · WEB-DL CHDWEB

scrape.nfoHint: tvshow.nfo / movie.nfo / episode NFOs, including tmdbid for exact identification
scrape.episodeStillsHint: One -thumb.jpg per episode; large shows write the most files, so this can be disabled separately
scrape.metadataLanguageHint: The language of titles, overviews and genre names. Select languages in priority order. The first sets the TMDB request language; missing fields fall back through translations already fetched, without extra requests.
scrape.contentRatingHint: Use the first region with a rating available, such as PG-13 or TV-MA.
scrape.imageSourcesHint: Choose posters, backdrops, title logos and season posters from multiple sources. TMDB is always enabled. Fanart.tv is a community HD collection, often with more Chinese logos and season posters. Images you select manually on a title always take priority.
scrape.primarySource: Primary source for metadata and images
scrape.sharedKeyHint: This key is shared across the server. Change it in Settings → Metadata and organization.
scrape.fanartConfiguredHint: Community HD artwork · Movies use TMDB IDs; TV shows use TVDB IDs (obtained automatically from TMDB)
scrape.fanartUnconfiguredHint: Community HD artwork · Enable it and enter your own API key once
scrape.fanartRejected: Fanart.tv rejected this key (it may be revoked or incorrect). Automatic Fanart image selection is paused.
scrape.sourceOrderHint: Set each image type separately; click ⇄ to swap
scrape.defaultPosterHint: Poster mode is “TMDB default”: compare its single selected poster with Fanart posters by language
scrape.seasonPosterHint: TV shows only; follows the poster language priority
scrape.estimateAfterSave: Save to estimate the selected sizes
scrape.posterHint: Posters have languages too: Chinese, original and textless artwork are separate candidates. Images you select manually on a title always take priority.
scrape.defaultPosterDescription: Matches Discover; the poster stays the same before and after subscribing (default)
scrape.languagePosterDescription: Use the first language with candidates, then rank by resolution and votes
scrape.fanartPosterHint: Fanart.tv is enabled: compare TMDB’s default poster with Fanart posters using the language order above. Replace it only if Fanart has a poster in a higher priority language. Season posters follow this order too.
scrape.backdropHint: Full screen artwork behind title details. “Textless” means no embedded title text; put it first for clean images. Put a language first if you prefer backdrops with a title logo.
scrape.logoHint: A title wordmark with a transparent background, shown over artwork on the home and detail pages. Use the first available language; if none is found, show the text title instead.
scrape.minResolutionHint: Controls which image is selected: reject images below this width, relaxing the limit if none qualify. “Local image quality” below controls the stored size.
scrape.localQualityHint: The size stored locally during metadata fetching. The server scales this image down for each device, so this sets its maximum detail. Refresh metadata in a library to update existing images after a quality change.
scrape.loadFailed: Could not load. Please try again.
scrape.saveFailed: Could not save. Please try again.
scrape.metadataSectionHint: Language for titles and overviews, and regions for content ratings
scrape.imagesSectionHint: Artwork sources, language priorities and local image sizes
scrape.namingSectionHint: Directory and file names used when importing
scrape.mirrorSectionHint: Write scraping results into media directories for Emby / Jellyfin / Kodi. Only add files; never delete or overwrite existing NFOs. Each library also has a master switch.
scrape.globalLoadFailed: Could not load global metadata settings
scrape.libraryIntro: Metadata fetching preferences for this library. Unchanged settings follow Settings → Metadata and organization.
scrape.libraryNamingHint: Leave blank to follow the global template. Each library can use its own names within its directory tree. See Settings → Metadata and organization → Naming templates for all tokens (original title, episode title, video codec, site and more) and a live preview.
scrape.libraryMirrorHint: Write scraping results into this library’s media directory. The master switch in Basic information overrides these three settings when disabled.
scrape.fanartGlobalTitle: Enter your Fanart.tv API key once
scrape.fanartGlobalBody: Fanart.tv requires your own API key (available with free registration). Enter it once to use it here, in library settings and in image selection dialogs across the server.
scrape.fanartLibraryTitle: Enter an API key to use Fanart.tv in this library
scrape.fanartLibraryBody: The key is saved for the entire server. Global settings and other libraries can use it without entering it again.
scrape.fanartModalBody: Enter your own Fanart.tv API key once (available with free registration). You can then choose images here immediately. Automatic use of Fanart still depends on the settings switch.
scrape.fanartVerifyFailed: Verification failed. Please try again later.
scrape.fanartGetKey: Get a free key at fanart.tv ↗
scrape.fanartVipHint: VIP keys get access to newly uploaded images sooner
scrape.defaultFanartComparison: TMDB default · Compare with Fanart by {languages}
scrape.priorityHint: Fall back in this order (up to {max})
scrape.overrideLibrariesCount: {count, plural, one {# library override} other {# library overrides}}
scrape.fanartEnabledHint: Fanart.tv is enabled. New titles use it automatically. Refresh metadata in the library for existing titles to select artwork from the new sources; otherwise their images stay unchanged.
scrape.languageBeforeSource: Language takes priority over source. Each image type follows its own language order, configured in the poster, backdrop and title logo cards. Source order breaks ties within the same language. Putting Chinese first keeps source order from choosing English artwork instead.
scrape.globalIntro: Server defaults for metadata fetching. Changes save automatically and apply to new metadata fetching immediately. Refresh metadata in a library to update existing titles. Every setting can be overridden under Edit library → Metadata settings; other libraries follow these defaults.
scrape.ownershipHint: Metadata language and artwork belong to a title: one record and one poster per title. They follow the title’s metadata owner library, so these settings apply only to titles owned by this library. Refresh metadata here to apply changes to existing titles.

Enable a proxy as needed. “Test” sends a real request using the current settings; a successful test immediately restores a service whose circuit breaker is open.

proxy.mirrorExplanation: There are two independent ways to reach TMDB: a proxy changes the network route while keeping the destination, and a mirror replaces the official destination with a directly reachable reverse proxy. Choose either if possible. If both are configured, requests go through the proxy to the mirror. Mirrors may be self-hosted with nginx or Cloudflare Workers, or public. Public mirrors can see your API key.

If you only want a different access port, change the left-hand side of the mapping instead.
